paragraphs.text: "The trick to getting the biggest share is to be the last one standing."
Unlike their pack-hunting kin, ferocidons stalk in solitude and lash out at everything that approaches.
Outsiders may marvel at the Sun Empire's "domesticated" dinosaurs, but those who live alongside them know they can never truly be tamed.
If you see one, you're already surrounded.
"When you go where the currents take you, you'll never run short of things to discover."
Many of the ancient civilizations beneath Ixalan were destroyed by outside forces. Others tapped into power they found they could not control.
"It is one thing to run away. It is quite another to escape your fate." —Oko
"It's downright selfish to die with full pockets."
"We're taking back what's ours. And a little bit of what's yours."
"These people come from their cities and think to tame the wilderness. They forget that here, the wilderness has a head start." —Selvala
Travelers who have reached the headwaters of Fool's Fall say that strange serpents dwell in the waters there, though none can recall any more than that.
"All these childhood memories are getting in the way of the vault codes."
"Only a fool goes out there unprepared. If the heat doesn't get you, the time alone with your thoughts likely will." —Ertha Jo, frontier mentor
When Kellan let his eyes wander to the horizon, he saw a land whose destiny was as uncertain as his own.
Its gaze gifts you with knowledge no mortal mind should possess.
Sagas sing of realms long forgotten, shattered by doomskars and cleaved violently from the World Tree.

"No one has heard Drivnod speak. But we have seen him do unspeakable things. As he drifts over Ish Sah, a deathly whisper rides the wind. I can never watch for long—I turn away and hide." —Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster
"I paid a price to one I will not name to escape the abyss. A bit of my soul for a second chance. And I'd do it again, and again—until I had no soul left to trade." —Tinua, Skirsdag cultist
"Art exposes truth. Each step of my dance brings me closer to the secrets of the universe."
"I'm not as quick as I used to be, but the wheat doesn't mind."
"Pah! You call this a comprehensive? I call this nest-stuffing!"
For every five you see, there are fifty you don't.
Each of them is a bad influence on the rest.
"Anyone can live next door, but when you fight to defend your neighbors, you become a village." —Rho, veteran hero
The magic of the land is a thread that weaves all of Valley into a tapestry, connecting even the most distant of friends.
"It started as a prototype for a frog diving suit, but the internal mechanisms didn't leave room for the frog." —Fitzwhisker, otterfolk inventor
The group called the Benefactors offers what aid and protection it can to other survivors, marking precious safe zones with the sign of the flame.
Even those who think they have nothing have something left to lose.
Bound to a single house, Valgavoth simply expanded its boundaries until it consumed the plane, turning a vibrant world into his playground of terror.
Cultists eagerly undergo the Rite of the Threshold, allowing Valgavoth to feed on their fear and bind them to the essence of the House.
He turns every room into a crematorium.
Survivors who stay together, slay together.
"Nothing I beat down stays down. I love this place!" —Tyvar
"Cyclical as the passing of days, the fiend would return again. And like the sun rising, so would a champion to slay it." —*Heroics: A Book of Fables*
Sailors swear by the Sphinx's stars, which always seem to point the way home.
"I freely trade away my breaths, for the only one I must keep is my last." —Sopia, Skelle cleric
"Follow me. I know these hills like the back of my stabbing knife."
Within sky-scraping gardens, New Capenna's fashionable druids maintain the last ties to the war-ravaged land their ancestors left behind.
"Hello again, my metamorphic friends. What stories have you brought to tell me today?"
"Those who do evil shall face wrath unrelenting." —Memorial inscription
"Proper chronomancy research can't be rushed. Luckily, I've got all the time in the world."
"Exist in the moment. Ignore the world around you. Embrace the one truth of reality, that all life is motion."
"I scream, you scream, we all scream... forever."
"Where do you think you're going, chum?"
Ferren Gibrar's award-winning invention from the Inventor's Fair-now available to the general public.
Engineers take inspiration form nature when it comes to efficiency and aerodynamics. Why not intimidation too?
"We are the voice of the untethered and lost ancestors. The memory of the Abzan. We guide those that yet live." —Betor
"I will give you a fair and beautiful judgment." —Teval
"We sing and the chorus of creation responds." —Ureni
"The Way tells us we must strive towards unity of mind. Through shared understanding, we may yet put an end to strife on Tarkir." —Shiko
"Strength comes from community. Together, we can destroy any enemy." —Neriv
"This was where I fought my first battle under Kolaghan. How I have outgrown her." —Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
"We remember all the world has endured, everything it has gone through to bring us to today. We are proud of Tarkir." —Betor
In the mist, turbulent enough to deafen. Beneath the boughs, serene enough to soothe.
"I came here often to meditate on Ojutai's teachings. Now, I must also consider his failings." —Narset
Where dragonlords once schemed, their memory now dissipates.
With every morningtide, Eirdu sheds a single wish for one lucky enough to catch it.
The thoughtweft guides his hands with the will of an entire clachan, so his strikes land ever true.
"It's true, the more painful the sacrifice, the more beautiful the outcome. What would you give for your desires to become reality?" —Maralen, fae ascendant
She is drawn to those dreams found only in the eternal sleep.
Rotscab looked ridiculous, and his warren-mates were unbearably envious.
Shadowmoor boggarts fondly remember their first kill. And their second. And their third . . .
For one glorious moment, the flamekin's heart showed him his blazing potential.
Lasting beauty is to give more than you take.
"Change is hard, but necessary. We must realize a world in which elves are guided not by superiority but by harmony."
Not as old as the yews, nor as strong as the giants, nor as discerning as the elves, yet lord over them all.
"No, Oona was not the source of this world's magic. I hear the land's heart beating to a more primal rhythm."
During the Invasion, the Phyrexians agreed there were some things that were not worth *compleating*.
Few giants remember the magic woven into the stone gates, the final gift of a wandering ascetic who died eons ago.
A wandering palette seeking a master's hand to give it purpose.
Was it a thousand years old, or would it make you live for a thousand years? The boggart didn't ask.
Droplets of an idea pool, until the dam breaks and the flood is unleashed.
Replace the broken now, mend the cracks in the foundation.
Walls to hold the unsightly past at bay, a new truth painted within.
A moment's pause, doubt chips away the facade, the thin veneer exposed.
The doubt expunged, the walls restored, memory molded like clay.
The clay is nothing without a hand to shape, the shape yielding until forged in fire.
A new foundation. A new beginning. But still, cracks. Cracks leaking a thought, an idea.
